meta.title: The Best Snapdrop Alternative for Any Network | BIShare
meta.description: A Snapdrop alternative that works off-network too: send files locally like Snapdrop, or share a browser link + code when devices aren't on the same Wi-Fi. Free, no account.

hero.title: A Snapdrop alternative for any network
hero.body: Snapdrop and PairDrop are brilliant for a quick drop between two browsers — until the devices aren't on the same network, or you want a real app. BIShare keeps the local, no-account simplicity but adds off-network sending through a browser link, plus native apps for every platform. Same Wi-Fi or not, it just works.

why.title: Where Snapdrop stops
why.body: Snapdrop — and its successor PairDrop — connects two browsers through your local network, so both devices have to sit on the same Wi-Fi, and there's no background app to resume a big transfer. The moment you're on mobile data, a guest network, or across town, it can't help. BIShare covers that gap: direct transfers when you're together, and a browser link with a 6-character code when you're not.

how.title: How BIShare sends, near or far

0.b: Pick the device and send — files go straight across, end-to-end encrypted, with nothing stored on a server. Just like Snapdrop, but faster through a native app, and it even works over a phone hotspot with no internet.

1.b: This is the part Snapdrop can't do. You get a link, a QR code, and a 6-character code. The other person opens the link in any browser and downloads — no app, no sign-up. The link auto-expires in 24 hours.

2.b: iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac, and Linux — one native app instead of a browser tab. Send from your phone to your laptop, or to anyone, in any direction.

rows.r1: Native apps, not just a browser tab
rows.r2: Resumable large files up to 100 GB

0.a: BIShare. It keeps what people love about Snapdrop — instant local transfers, no account, works in a browser — and adds what Snapdrop can't do: sending when devices are on different networks, native apps for every platform, and end-to-end encryption on every transfer.

1.q: Is Snapdrop still working? What happened to it?
1.a: The original Snapdrop was discontinued after being acquired, and its domain now points elsewhere. PairDrop is the open-source community successor most people use today. Both are same-network only — BIShare works the same way locally but also handles the off-network case with a share link.

2.q: Can a Snapdrop-style app work when devices aren't on the same Wi-Fi?
2.a: Not the classic Snapdrop way — it pairs two browsers over the local network, so both devices must share the same Wi-Fi. BIShare removes that limit: when you're on different networks, it gives you a link and a 6-character code the other person opens in any browser to download.

3.q: Is BIShare more secure than Snapdrop or PairDrop?
3.a: BIShare encrypts every transfer end-to-end, and local transfers never touch a server at all. Snapdrop and PairDrop use browser WebRTC, which is encrypted in transit but relies on a signaling server to connect. With BIShare, share links also expire automatically after 24 hours.

4.a: Yes. BIShare is free with no account, just like Snapdrop. Local transfers over your own network have no size caps, share links handle files up to 100 GB, and the person receiving never has to install or sign up for anything.

cta.title: A Snapdrop that follows you off the network
cta.body: Free, no account. Keep the instant local drop, add native apps and a share link for when you're apart — and the other side still needs nothing but a browser.
